eventMetadata.context_description: An intense heatwave driven by the North Pacific High has produced record subsidence warming, clear skies, and elevated humidity across southeastern South Korea, positioning Busan for daily highs near or above 38°C on August 1. The July 29 official reading of 38.8°C—the city’s highest since 1904—demonstrates the current anomaly’s strength, with nearby stations exceeding 40°C and KMA heat advisories remaining active. Maritime moisture from the surrounding seas limits nighttime cooling and sustains high apparent temperatures, while typical August baselines of 29–32°C have been sharply exceeded. These conditions support trader consensus around the 38–40°C range, though any strengthening of onshore flow or increased cloud cover could moderate the peak.
